question.problem: Find the equation of the tangent to the curve $f(x)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(4-2x)$ at the point $(1,\operatorname{ln}⁡2).$
question.worked_solution:
First, we express $f(x)$ as the composite function

$$
f=\operatorname{ln}⁡u,\,u=4-2x.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}=\frac{1}{u},\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-2.
$$

We now apply the chain rule, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & =\frac{1}{u}\cdot (-2) \\  & =\frac{1}{4-2x}\cdot (-2) \\  & =-\frac{2}{4-2x} \\  & =-\frac{\cancel{2}}{\cancel{2}\cdot (2-x)} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2-x}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope $m$ of the tangent line at the point where $x=1$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=1} & ={-\frac{1}{2-x}|}_{x=1}=-\frac{1}{2-1}=-1\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the slope of the tangent line at the point $(1,\operatorname{ln}⁡2)$ is $m=-1.$ Now, we find the equation of the tangent at that point:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-\operatorname{ln}⁡2 & =-1(x-1) \\ y & =-x+1+\operatorname{ln}⁡2\end{aligned}
$$
